summary: Observation of the NE-SW passage of a red ball in the sky and fragmentation: probable observation of the passage of a bolide.
description: On November 15, 1956, at 7:05 PM in Paris, a pilot observed a bright red ball moving from northwest to southeast across the clear sky. A second ball detached from it and followed a downward parabolic trajectory for one second. No trail was observed. Both balls suddenly and simultaneously disappeared. Only one eyewitness account was recorded at the time. GEIPAN classified this event as category B: probable observation of a fireball caused by the reentry into the atmosphere of a natural meteoroid that fragmented.

summary: Observations by pilots of the movement of an aluminium coloured spherical object: probable observation of a stratospheric balloon.
description: On September 20, 1956, at 3:50 PM, two pilots from a patrol aircraft observed the movement of an aluminum-colored spherical object. Intrigued and intending to get closer, the pilots gained altitude but realized it was impossible to reach it. They abandoned the pursuit at 4:10 PM. Following an inquiry to the director of the Puy-de-Dôme Observatory in Clermont-Ferrand (63), it was discovered that a translucent balloon, approximately spherical in shape with a slight bulge at its base, had been observed throughout the day of September 20 in the skies above Clermont-Ferrand. It drifted continuously at a very low speed at an altitude of 20 km before becoming invisible at 7:05 PM, no longer illuminated by the sun. The observatory did not know the origin of the object, stating that neither the regional weather services nor they themselves had conducted any balloon launches. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: observation of a stratospheric balloon whose origin could not be determined. The impression of being followed by the object and the inability to get closer are characteristic of perceptual illusions when observing distant objects. In our case, the very large balloon was approximately 17 km from the pilots. Approaching it at an altitude of 32,000 feet (10,000 meters) only reduced this distance by about 10 km, which is still significant.

summary: Observations by two groups of witnesses of two round and red shaped phenomena in the sky: lack of information.
description: On April 8, 1956, at approximately 11:40-11:45 PM, three witnesses in the town of La Londe (76) observed a red sphere in the direction of the west during a clear, moonless night. The phenomenon appeared stationary for several minutes, then seemed to move as the witnesses moved. The phenomenon disappeared behind the trees. The observation lasted about twenty minutes. The gendarmerie collected three other testimonies for the same date and at 11:30-11:45 PM: these witnesses, in a car in Elbeuf (76), described a round, red shape in motion. The observation was very brief (4 to 5 seconds) in the direction of Orival (76). The available information does not confirm that the two groups saw the same phenomenon. Astronomical verification indicates that for the first group, Venus was near the horizon, approximately 45° north of the direction of observation, and for the second group, looking north, no particular celestial body was visible. This case is not very strange and the information is too imprecise: GEIPAN classifies this case as C.
